title: سوائل الحفر وأثرها في كفاءة الحفر وسلامة البئر: تجربة تطبيقية في الحقول الليبية Drilling Fluids and Their Impact on Drilling Efficiency and Wellbore Integrity: An Applied Experience in Libyan Fields
journal: Derna Academy Journal for Applied Sciences
abstract: تتناول هذه الورقة دور سوائل الحفر في رفع كفاءة حفر الآبار النفطية وصون سلامتها في ظل الظروف الجيولوجية والتشغيلية التي تواجه الحقول الليبية. اعتمدت الدراسة منهجاً وصفياً تحليلياً جمع بين مراجعة منظمة للأدبيات المحكّمة الحديثة في الريولوجيا واستقرار البئر وفقد الدورة والإضافات المستحدثة، وبين قراءة تحليلية للخبرة التشغيلية للباحث التي تمتد عشرين عاماً في هندسة سوائل الحفر على الحفارات. وخلصت الورقة إلى أن عدم استقرار البئر في التكوينات الطينية ينشأ عن تفاعل ميكانيكي كيميائي لا يعالجه السائل وحده، بل يتطلب تصميمه في ضوء نموذج جيوميكانيكي للتكوين؛ وأن الخصائص الريولوجية للسائل تتغير بتغير الحرارة والضغط، فلا يكفي الاعتماد على القياسات السطحية؛ وأن اختيار نوع السائل مفاضلة بين الأداء والتكلفة والأثر البيئي. وتقدم الورقة إطاراً عملياً يربط المشكلات الشائعة بإجراءات سوائلية محددة، وتوصي ببناء نماذج جيوميكانيكية للآبار الجديدة، واختبار السوائل في ظروف القاع، وتوثيق بيانات الآبار المجاورة، وإجراء تجارب حقلية محدودة قبل تعميم الإضافات الحديثة.

title: Transforming Organizational Culture Through Leadership and Learning: A Framework for Employee Engagement, Innovation, and Sustainable Performance
journal: Journal of Business Practice and Academic Research
abstract: Organizations face continuous pressure to adapt to technological change, evolving workforce expectations, competitive intensity, and rising demands for sustainable performance, yet leadership development, learning, culture change, engagement, innovation, and sustainability are typically designed and evaluated as separate initiatives. This conceptual article develops an integrative framework explaining how transformational leadership and organizational learning jointly drive organizational culture transformation, and how a transformed culture supports sustainable performance through the complementary pathways of employee engagement and organizational innovation. The study adopts an integrative literature review and theory synthesis design, drawing on four complementary lenses: Transformational Leadership Theory, Organizational Learning Theory, Social Exchange Theory, and the Dynamic Capabilities perspective. title: Theorizing Instructional Assistant Practice in Inclusive Classrooms
journal: Journal of Humanities and Social Policy
abstract: Instructional assistants, known variously as paraprofessionals, teaching assistants, or educational support staff, have become the single largest category of adults supporting learners with disabilities in inclusive classrooms across most English-speaking and internationally comparable education systems. Despite that numerical predominance, the literature on Individualized Education Program (IEP) delivery has continued to treat teachers and specialist therapists as the primary agents of planning and implementation, with paraprofessionals occupying a secondary and frequently under-specified role. This paper proposes a conceptual framework that re-centres the instructional assistant as a co-deliverer of the IEP, while preserving the accountability and pedagogical leadership of the qualified teacher and specialist team. The framework, which is derived through the integration of the international paraprofessional research literature, the evidence base on IEP implementation, and the practitioner-oriented literature on inclusive special education, identifies four interlocking domains in which paraprofessionals contribute to IEP delivery: instructional delivery, behavioural scaffolding, communication support, and data collection. Each domain is specified in terms of observable practice, required competencies, supervisory structures, and ethical safeguards. The framework is distinguished from prior roletaxonomies by its explicit attention to the decision-making discretion exercised by paraprofessionals in the moment-to-moment classroom life of the learner, and by its insistence that paraprofessional practice be theorised rather than catalogued. Implications are drawn for teacher-paraprofessional collaboration, for paraprofessional preparation programmes, and for the evaluation of IEP implementation quality. The paper concludes that treating paraprofessionals as passive executors of plans designed elsewhere is both empirically inaccurate and pedagogically costly.

title: The Rise of Mouth Taping and the Role of the Dental Profession
Temporal Infrastructure in Special Education: Routines, Visuals, and Transitions
journal: International Journal of Education and Evaluation
abstract: Classroom management is the institutional infrastructure through which the conditions for teaching and learning are established and sustained in the classroom. The construct has been developed primarily within general education research, but its adaptation to the distinctive conditions of the special education classroom requires sustained attention to the specific features of that setting: the wider range of developmental profiles, the more pronounced sensory and behavioural variability, the greater reliance on multi-adult teams, and the closer integration of routine with the individualised programmes through which the learners are served. This paper synthesises the conceptual and empirical literature on three interlocking strands of special education classroom management: the organisation of classroom routines as the temporal architecture of the school day, the use of visual schedules as cognitive and communicative supports that render the routine accessible to learners with varied processing profiles, and the structured support of transitions between activities, between settings, and across longer-duration changes. The paper traces the foundational work on which contemporary practice rests, examines the empirical base for each strand, articulates the mechanisms through which the three strands operate jointly, and considers the implementation considerations that shape the success of classroom management in real settings. The paper is explicitly conceptual; no primary data are presented, and its claims are offered as a scaffold for further research and for the coherent design of pedagogical programmes

title: Inclusive Self-Efficacy and Paraprofessional Collaboration: An Integrated Framework
journal: Research Journal of Humanities and Cultural Studies
abstract: Teacher self-efficacy, the educator's belief in her capacity to organise and execute the courses of action required to produce specified instructional attainments, has emerged as one of the most generative constructs in the educational psychology of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries. When applied to inclusive classrooms serving learners with disabilities, the construct both illuminates and complicates the relationship between belief and practice. Inclusive selfefficacy is structured by the educator's perceived competence across instructional, behavioural, and collaborative domains, and the collaborative domain has become increasingly salient as paraprofessional staff has assumed a central role in the daily implementation of inclusive education. This paper synthesises the conceptual and empirical literature on teacher self-efficacy for inclusive practice with the emerging literature on paraprofessional-teacher collaboration, with a view to specifying how the two bodies of work can inform one another. The paper traces the genealogy of the self-efficacy construct within social cognitive theory, examines its specialisation as inclusive self-efficacy, identifies the principal correlates and antecedents documented in the empirical literature, and articulates the role of the paraprofessional workforce in the efficacypractice relationship. Particular attention is given to the mechanisms through which collaborative practice generates, sustains, or erodes inclusive self-efficacy for both categories of adult. The paper is explicitly conceptual, and its arguments are offered as an organising framework for further empirical and theoretical work.

title: Who Plans to Marry? Economic Security and Marital Intentions Among Never‐Married Adults in Türkiye
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To examine how three dimensions of economic security, namely employment position, wealth, and income, are associated with the marital intentions of never‐married adults in Türkiye, and to formally test whether these associations differ by gender. Background Marriage remains the dominant pathway to family formation in Türkiye, yet marriage is increasingly postponed amid economic uncertainty. Existing policy measures largely target the immediate costs of marrying rather than the underlying economic security that shapes whether marriage is perceived as feasible. Method By using the 2016 Türkiye Family Structure Survey, ordered logit models are estimated separately by gender and reported as average marginal effects on the probability of intending to marry; gender differences are tested formally in pooled models interacting gender with all covariates. Results Public‐sector employment is associated with higher marital intentions and student status with lower intentions for both genders, whereas labor‐market inactivity predicts lower intentions only among men. Car and other‐asset ownership are positively associated with men's, but not women's intentions, although gender differences in these differences are not statistically distinguishable. Significant gender differences emerge instead in education. Tertiary‐educated women are more likely, and tertiary‐educated men less likely, to intend to marry relative to their less‐educated counterparts. Conclusion Employment‐based security is the most consistent correlate of marital intentions for both women and men, consistent with uncertainty‐based accounts of marriage timing. Implications Policies that foster stable employment and predictable labor‐market entry for young adults may be more relevant to family formation than measures targeting wedding costs alone.
